pattern: あげる / くれる / もらう
formation_reference_en: Noun (receiver) + に + Noun + を + あげる / Noun (giver) + が + Noun + を + くれる / Noun (giver) + に + Noun + を + もらう
meaning_reference_en: give (to someone else); give (to me or my group); receive
notes_reference_en: くれる is used only when the receiver is the speaker or someone in the speaker's group. With もらう the giver can be marked with に or から.

formation_reference_en: Verb-te + あげる
meaning_reference_en: do something for someone (as a favor)
notes_reference_en: Said directly to a superior it can sound condescending; use the humble お〜しましょうか (お持ちしましょうか) instead.

formation_reference_en: Verb-te + くれる
meaning_reference_en: someone does something for me (or my group)
notes_reference_en: The subject is the person doing the favor; the one who benefits is the speaker or someone close to them.

formation_reference_en: Verb-te + もらう
meaning_reference_en: have someone do something (for me); get someone to do
notes_reference_en: The receiver of the favor is the subject, and the person who does the action is marked with に.

formation_reference_en: Verb-te + くださる / Verb-te + いただく
meaning_reference_en: (honorific) someone kindly does for me; (humble) I receive the favor of someone doing
notes_reference_en: くださる is the honorific version of くれる (ます-form: くださいます); いただく is the humble version of もらう.

formation_reference_en: Verb-te + いく
meaning_reference_en: do something and go; go on doing (from now into the future)
notes_reference_en: Movement or change away from the speaker, or from now toward the future. Compare 〜てくる.

formation_reference_en: Verb-te + くる
meaning_reference_en: do something and come back; come doing; (change) up to now; start to
notes_reference_en: Movement or change toward the speaker, or from the past up to now. 行ってきます literally means 'I'll go and come back.'

formation_reference_en: Verb-te + しまう
meaning_reference_en: finish completely; do by accident; end up doing (with regret)
notes_reference_en: In speech 〜てしまう contracts to 〜ちゃう, and 〜でしまう to 〜じゃう (飲んじゃう).

formation_reference_en: Verb-te + おく
meaning_reference_en: do in advance (to prepare); do and leave as is
notes_reference_en: In casual speech 〜ておく often becomes 〜とく (買っとく), and 〜でおく becomes 〜どく (読んどく).

formation_reference_en: Verb-te + みる
meaning_reference_en: try doing (to see what it is like)
notes_reference_en: Means trying something out to see the result, not making an effort to do something difficult.

formation_reference_en: Verb-te + ある
meaning_reference_en: has been done (and stays that way); resulting state of a deliberate action
notes_reference_en: Used with transitive verbs, and the object usually takes が. It implies someone did it on purpose, unlike 〜ている with intransitive verbs (窓が開いている).

formation_reference_en: Verb-plain / i-Adj / na-Adj + な / Noun + の + とき
meaning_reference_en: when; at the time when
notes_reference_en: The verb's tense shows the order: 行くとき means before or on the way (the going isn't finished yet); 行ったとき means after arriving. Often written 時 in kanji.

formation_reference_en: Verb-te + いる / Verb-dict / Noun + の + 間（に）
meaning_reference_en: while; during (the whole time); at some point during
notes_reference_en: 間 means the action continues through the whole period; 間に means it happens at some point within the period.

formation_reference_en: Verb-stem / i-Adj stem / na-Adj + そうだ
meaning_reference_en: looks like; seems; looks about to
notes_reference_en: A judgment from what you see. いい → よさそう, ない → なさそう. Not used with adjectives for plainly visible traits (赤い, かわいい); かわいそう means 'pitiful'.

formation_reference_en: Verb-plain / i-Adj + そうだ / na-Adj + だ + そうだ / Noun + だ + そうだ
meaning_reference_en: I heard that; they say that
notes_reference_en: Attaches to full plain forms, unlike the 'looks like' そうだ, which attaches to stems. It has no past or negative form.

formation_reference_en: Verb-plain / i-Adj / na-Adj / Noun + らしい
meaning_reference_en: apparently; it seems; I hear
notes_reference_en: Based on something heard or read, so the speaker sounds a little detached. The 'typical of' らしい (男らしい) is a separate N3 point.

formation_reference_en: Verb-plain / i-Adj + ようだ / na-Adj + な + ようだ / Noun + の + ようだ
meaning_reference_en: it seems; it appears (judging from evidence)
notes_reference_en: A somewhat formal way to state a judgment from what you observe or feel; みたいだ is the casual equivalent. The 'like, as if' use is covered at N3.

formation_reference_en: Verb-plain / i-Adj / na-Adj / Noun + みたい
meaning_reference_en: seems like; looks like; like (casual)
notes_reference_en: Casual equivalent of ようだ. It attaches directly to nouns and na-adjectives (静かみたい) without な or の. Before a noun it becomes みたいな.

formation_reference_en: Verb-stem / i-Adj stem / na-Adj + すぎる
meaning_reference_en: too; too much; excessively
notes_reference_en: Conjugates like a Group 2 verb (すぎた, すぎて). いい → よすぎる, and the adjective ない → なさすぎる.

formation_reference_en: Verb-stem + 方
meaning_reference_en: how to; way of doing
notes_reference_en: The result is a noun, so the object takes の instead of を (日本語の話し方). With する-verbs: 勉強のしかた.

formation_reference_en: Noun + 中
meaning_reference_en: in the middle of; during (ちゅう); throughout; all over (じゅう)
notes_reference_en: ちゅう marks an ongoing activity or a period (会議中, 午前中, 今週中); じゅう means 'throughout' a time or place (一日中, 世界中).

formation_reference_en: Verb-dict / Verb-nai + つもり
meaning_reference_en: intend to; plan to
notes_reference_en: States a firm personal intention. 〜つもりはない means 'have no intention of'. Asking a superior 〜つもりですか can sound blunt.

formation_reference_en: Verb-dict + 予定 / Noun + の + 予定
meaning_reference_en: plan to; be scheduled to
notes_reference_en: Refers to a fixed schedule or arrangement, often involving other people; more objective than つもり.

formation_reference_en: Verb-dict / Verb-nai + ことにする
meaning_reference_en: decide to
notes_reference_en: A decision made by the speaker; compare 〜ことになる. 〜ことにしている (N3) means 'make it a rule to'.

formation_reference_en: Verb-dict / Verb-nai + ことになる
meaning_reference_en: it has been decided that; it turns out that
notes_reference_en: Presents a decision as made by others or by circumstances. People also use it for their own decisions to sound less assertive.

formation_reference_en: Verb-dict + ことができる
meaning_reference_en: can; be able to; be possible to
notes_reference_en: A bit more formal than the potential form. Also used for what is possible or allowed (ここでたばこを吸うことはできません).

formation_reference_en: Verb-dict (Group 1: final u → e) + る / Verb-nai stem + られる (Group 2)
meaning_reference_en: can; be able to (potential form)
notes_reference_en: Irregular: する → できる, 来る → 来られる. The object often takes が instead of を. In casual speech Group 2 verbs often drop ら (見れる).

formation_reference_en: Verb-nai stem + れる (Group 1) / Verb-nai stem + られる (Group 2)
meaning_reference_en: be done (by someone); passive voice
notes_reference_en: Irregular: する → される, 来る → 来られる. The doer is marked with に. Often shows that the subject was troubled by someone's action (雨に降られた).

formation_reference_en: Verb-nai stem + せる (Group 1) / Verb-nai stem + させる (Group 2)
meaning_reference_en: make someone do; let someone do (causative)
notes_reference_en: Irregular: する → させる, 来る → 来させる. With intransitive verbs the person takes を; with transitive verbs, に. Context decides 'make' or 'let'.

formation_reference_en: Verb-nai stem + せられる (Group 1; short form される) / Verb-nai stem + させられる (Group 2)
meaning_reference_en: be made to do (against one's will)
notes_reference_en: Irregular: する → させられる, 来る → 来させられる. The short Group 1 form (待たされる) is common in speech, but not with verbs ending in す (話させられる).

formation_reference_en: Verb-dict (Group 1: final u → o) + う / Verb-stem + よう (Group 2)
meaning_reference_en: let's (casual); I'll (volitional form)
notes_reference_en: Irregular: する → しよう, 来る → 来よう. The plain equivalent of 〜ましょう.

formation_reference_en: Verb-volitional + と思う
meaning_reference_en: be thinking of doing; plan to
notes_reference_en: 〜と思う often reports a decision made just now; 〜と思っている shows a plan held for some time. Softer than つもり.

formation_reference_en: Verb-dict (Group 1: final u → e) / Verb-stem + ろ (Group 2)
meaning_reference_en: do it! (imperative form; blunt command)
notes_reference_en: Irregular: する → しろ, 来る → 来い, くれる → くれ. Very blunt; heard mainly from men, on signs, in emergencies and in cheering (がんばれ).

formation_reference_en: Verb-dict + な
meaning_reference_en: don't! (strong prohibition)
notes_reference_en: Very strong and blunt. Do not confuse it with the sentence-ending な that expresses feeling (いいな).

formation_reference_en: Verb-stem + なさい
meaning_reference_en: do (instruction from a parent, teacher, etc.)
notes_reference_en: Softer than the imperative form but still a firm instruction; used by parents, teachers and in exam directions, never toward superiors.

formation_reference_en: Verb-ba / i-Adj stem + ければ / na-Adj + なら / Noun + なら
meaning_reference_en: if
notes_reference_en: Focuses on the condition needed for a result. When the main clause is a request or invitation, たら is usually more natural unless the ば-clause is a state (ある, いる, adjectives).

formation_reference_en: Verb-ta + ら / i-Adj stem + かったら / na-Adj + だったら / Noun + だったら
meaning_reference_en: if; when; after
notes_reference_en: The most versatile conditional and very common in speech. With events certain to happen it means 'when/after'.

formation_reference_en: Verb-plain / i-Adj / na-Adj / Noun + なら
meaning_reference_en: if (it's the case that); if you're talking about
notes_reference_en: Takes up what the listener said or a situation assumed to be true, then gives advice or an opinion. Unlike たら, the main action can come before the なら-clause.

formation_reference_en: Verb-dict / Verb-nai / i-Adj + と / na-Adj + だ + と / Noun + だ + と
meaning_reference_en: when; if; whenever (natural or automatic result)
notes_reference_en: For natural results, how machines work, directions and habits. The main clause cannot be a request, wish or invitation.

formation_reference_en: Verb-te + も / i-Adj-ku + ても / na-Adj + でも / Noun + でも
meaning_reference_en: even if; even though
notes_reference_en: With question words or いくら it means 'no matter ...' (何を食べても, いくら待っても).

formation_reference_en: Verb-plain / i-Adj + のに / na-Adj + な + のに / Noun + な + のに
meaning_reference_en: although; even though (with surprise or dissatisfaction)
notes_reference_en: Carries surprise, disappointment or complaint. The main clause cannot be a request or intention; use けど or ても there.

formation_reference_en: Verb-dict + のに / Noun + に
meaning_reference_en: for; in order to (with use, time or cost)
notes_reference_en: Usually followed by words like 使う, いい, 便利, 必要 or かかる. With a noun, just に is used (旅行に便利).

formation_reference_en: Verb-plain / i-Adj + ので / na-Adj + な + ので / Noun + な + ので
meaning_reference_en: because; since
notes_reference_en: Sounds softer and more objective than から, so it is preferred when giving reasons politely or apologizing.

formation_reference_en: Verb-te / i-Adj stem + くて / na-Adj + で / Noun + で
meaning_reference_en: because; so (cause of a feeling or state)
notes_reference_en: The second part is usually a feeling, a potential form or a result, not a request or intention (use から or ので for those). Negative: 〜なくて (会えなくて寂しい).

formation_reference_en: Verb-plain / i-Adj + し / na-Adj + だ + し / Noun + だ + し
meaning_reference_en: and what's more; and besides (listing reasons)
notes_reference_en: Lists several reasons or points. A single し hints that there are other reasons too.

formation_reference_en: Sentence + けど / けれども
meaning_reference_en: but; although; (soft lead-in)
notes_reference_en: More conversational than が; けれども is a little more formal than けど. Often used as a soft lead-in before a question or request.

formation_reference_en: Verb-dict / Verb-ta / Noun + の + ために
meaning_reference_en: in order to; for (the sake of); because of
notes_reference_en: For purpose, the verb must be something the subject can control (compare 〜ように). The 'because of' use sounds fairly formal.

formation_reference_en: Verb-dict / Verb-nai + ように
meaning_reference_en: so that; in order that
notes_reference_en: Used with verbs the subject can't directly control: potential forms, 分かる, 見える, negatives. For deliberate actions use ために.

formation_reference_en: Verb-dict / Verb-nai + ようにする
meaning_reference_en: try to; make sure to; make a habit of
notes_reference_en: 〜ようにしている describes a habit you keep up. Compare 〜ようになる, a change that comes about.

formation_reference_en: Verb-dict / Verb-nai + ようになる
meaning_reference_en: come to; reach the point where (change in ability or habit)
notes_reference_en: Often used with potential verbs. For 'no longer', 〜なくなる is usually more natural than 〜ないようになる.

formation_reference_en: Verb-te + ほしい / Verb-nai + で + ほしい
meaning_reference_en: want someone to do
notes_reference_en: The person you want to act is marked with に. Said to a superior it can sound demanding; 〜ていただきたいです is more polite.

formation_reference_en: Verb-stem + たがる
meaning_reference_en: (someone else) wants to
notes_reference_en: Used for other people, since you can't directly know their wishes. Current wishes are usually expressed with 〜たがっている.

formation_reference_en: i-Adj stem / na-Adj + がる
meaning_reference_en: (someone else) feels; shows signs of feeling
notes_reference_en: Turns feeling adjectives (怖い, 寂しい, ほしい) into verbs describing how others seem to feel. The object of the feeling takes を.

formation_reference_en: Verb-plain / i-Adj / na-Adj / Noun + かもしれない
meaning_reference_en: might; may; possibly
notes_reference_en: About 50% certainty or less. In casual speech it is often shortened to かも.

formation_reference_en: Verb-plain / i-Adj / na-Adj / Noun + だろう
meaning_reference_en: probably; I suppose (plain form of でしょう)
notes_reference_en: Common in writing and in men's casual speech; でしょう is the polite form. Often used with たぶん or きっと, or as 〜だろうと思う.

formation_reference_en: Verb-plain / i-Adj + はずだ / na-Adj + な + はずだ / Noun + の + はずだ
meaning_reference_en: should be; is expected to (based on reasoning)
notes_reference_en: A confident expectation based on facts or logic, not a guess. It does not mean 'should' as a duty.

formation_reference_en: Verb-plain / i-Adj + はずがない / na-Adj + な + はずがない / Noun + の + はずがない
meaning_reference_en: can't be; there's no way that
notes_reference_en: Strong denial based on reasoning. 〜ないはずだ ('should not be') is a milder expectation.

formation_reference_en: Verb-plain / i-Adj + んです / na-Adj + な + んです / Noun + な + んです
meaning_reference_en: it's that ...; (explaining or asking for an explanation)
notes_reference_en: Adds a sense of explaining a situation or asking for the background. Casual forms are 〜んだ and 〜の. Overusing it can sound pushy.

formation_reference_en: Verb-plain / i-Adj / na-Adj / Noun + かどうか
meaning_reference_en: whether or not
notes_reference_en: Embeds a yes-no question in a sentence. For questions with a question word, use 〜か alone (何時に来るか).

formation_reference_en: Question word + ... + Verb-plain / i-Adj / na-Adj / Noun + か
meaning_reference_en: embedded question (what, where, who, etc.)
notes_reference_en: After a noun or na-adjective, だ is dropped (誰の傘か知らない).

formation_reference_en: Verb-plain / i-Adj + と思う / na-Adj + だ + と思う / Noun + だ + と思う
meaning_reference_en: I think that
notes_reference_en: Japanese usually negates the quoted clause (来ないと思う) rather than 思う. For another person's opinion, use 〜と思っている.

formation_reference_en: 「Sentence」 + と言う / Sentence (plain) + と言う
meaning_reference_en: say that; tell (quotation)
notes_reference_en: Direct quotes go inside 「」; indirect quotes use plain forms. 〜と言っていた is common when passing on what someone said.

formation_reference_en: Noun + しか + Verb-nai
meaning_reference_en: only; nothing but
notes_reference_en: Always paired with a negative verb. Compared with だけ, it stresses that the amount is small or not enough.

formation_reference_en: Noun + ばかり
meaning_reference_en: nothing but; only; all
notes_reference_en: Often implies there is too much of one thing. 〜てばかりいる (N3) and 〜たばかり ('just did') are separate points.

formation_reference_en: Verb-ta + ばかり
meaning_reference_en: have just done
notes_reference_en: Shows the speaker feels little time has passed, even if it was weeks ago. 〜たところ refers to only moments ago.

formation_reference_en: Verb-dict / Verb-te + いる / Verb-ta + ところだ
meaning_reference_en: be about to; be in the middle of; have just done
notes_reference_en: Dictionary form: about to. 〜ているところ: in the middle of. 〜たところ: just finished. It pinpoints the stage of an action.

formation_reference_en: Verb-stem + やすい / Verb-stem + にくい
meaning_reference_en: easy to; hard to
notes_reference_en: Both conjugate like i-adjectives. やすい can also mean 'tends to' (この服は汚れやすい).

formation_reference_en: Verb-stem + 始める / Verb-stem + 終わる / Verb-stem + 続ける
meaning_reference_en: start doing; finish doing; keep doing
notes_reference_en: 〜終わる is used with actions that have a clear end (読む, 食べる, 書く). 〜終える is a more formal alternative.

formation_reference_en: Verb-stem + 出す
meaning_reference_en: suddenly start doing; burst out
notes_reference_en: Implies a sudden, often uncontrolled start. Unlike 〜始める, it is not used for planned actions or in requests.

formation_reference_en: Noun / Verb-plain + ほど + i-Adj-ku + ない / na-Adj + ではない
meaning_reference_en: not as ... as
notes_reference_en: The item before ほど is the standard of comparison. Always followed by a negative.

formation_reference_en: なかなか + Verb-nai
meaning_reference_en: not easily; just won't; not readily
notes_reference_en: Shows that something doesn't happen as quickly or easily as hoped. With a positive form, なかなか means 'quite' (なかなかおいしい).

formation_reference_en: Noun (quantity) + ずつ
meaning_reference_en: each; at a time; little by little

formation_reference_en: Noun (number + counter) + も
meaning_reference_en: as many as; as much as; (with a negative) not even one
notes_reference_en: Shows the speaker feels the amount is large. With 一 + counter and a negative verb, it means 'not even one'.

formation_reference_en: Noun / Verb-dict + までに
meaning_reference_en: by (a deadline); before
notes_reference_en: までに marks a deadline for a one-time action; まで marks how long something continues (六時まで働く).

formation_reference_en: Verb-dict / Verb-nai + ことがある
meaning_reference_en: sometimes; there are times when
notes_reference_en: Takes the dictionary or ない form. With the past form (〜たことがある) it means 'have done before' instead.

formation_reference_en: Verb-nai + といけない / Verb-nai stem + なくちゃ
meaning_reference_en: have to; must (conversational)
notes_reference_en: Everyday alternatives to なければならない. なくちゃ comes from なくては; なきゃ (from なければ) is also very common.

formation_reference_en: Verb-nai stem + せてください (Group 1) / Verb-nai stem + させてください (Group 2)
meaning_reference_en: please let me (do)
notes_reference_en: Built on the causative て-form (する → させて). 〜させていただけませんか is more polite.

formation_reference_en: いらっしゃる（行く・来る・いる） / 召し上がる（食べる・飲む） / おっしゃる（言う） / なさる（する） / ご覧になる（見る） / くださる（くれる）
meaning_reference_en: honorific verbs; respectful language for others' actions
notes_reference_en: Raises the actions of people you respect, such as customers, teachers and superiors. Never use it for your own actions.

formation_reference_en: 参る（行く・来る） / おる（いる） / いただく（食べる・飲む・もらう） / 申す（言う） / いたす（する） / 拝見する（見る） / 伺う（聞く・訪ねる）
meaning_reference_en: humble verbs; modest language for one's own actions
notes_reference_en: Lowers your own actions, or your group's, toward someone you respect. 参る, おる, 申す and いたす also make speech sound formal in general.

formation_reference_en: お + Verb-stem + になる
meaning_reference_en: (honorific) someone respected does
notes_reference_en: Not used with one-syllable stems (見る, 寝る) or verbs that have special forms (行く → いらっしゃる). する-nouns take ご + Noun + になる (ご利用になる).

formation_reference_en: お + Verb-stem + する / ご + Noun + する
meaning_reference_en: (humble) I do (for someone respected)
notes_reference_en: Only for actions that affect or benefit the other person. お〜いたします is even more formal.

formation_reference_en: Noun / na-Adj + でございます
meaning_reference_en: is; am; are (very polite copula)
notes_reference_en: The very polite version of です, typical of shop and hotel staff speaking to customers. ございます on its own is the polite form of あります.

formation_reference_en: Verb-te + も構わない / i-Adj-ku + ても構わない / na-Adj + でも構わない / Noun + でも構わない
meaning_reference_en: don't mind if; it's fine if
notes_reference_en: A little more formal than 〜てもいい. 〜なくても構わない means 'it's fine not to'.

formation_reference_en: Verb-plain + の / Verb-plain + こと
meaning_reference_en: the act of doing (turns a verb phrase into a noun)
notes_reference_en: の is preferred with perception verbs (見る, 聞こえる) and in casual speech; こと is needed before です/だ and in set patterns such as 〜ことができる.

formation_reference_en: Verb-ba + よかった / Verb-nai stem + なければよかった
meaning_reference_en: should have (done); I wish I had
notes_reference_en: Expresses regret about the past. 〜たらよかった is a common conversational alternative.

formation_reference_en: Verb-ta + らどう
meaning_reference_en: why don't you ...?; how about ...?
notes_reference_en: Often shortened to 〜たら？. Can sound pushy toward superiors; 〜たらいかがですか is the polite version.

formation_reference_en: Verb-ta / Verb-nai + ほうがいい
meaning_reference_en: had better; should
notes_reference_en: For advice, the past form (行ったほうがいい) is the usual choice and sounds stronger. The negative uses the ない form, not the past.

formation_reference_en: Noun + とか + Noun + とか / Verb-dict + とか + Verb-dict + とか
meaning_reference_en: things like A and B; A, B and so on (casual)
notes_reference_en: More casual than 〜や〜など, and it can also list verbs or whole phrases.

formation_reference_en: Noun + など
meaning_reference_en: etc.; and so on; such as
notes_reference_en: Often paired with や (AやBなど). After a single noun it softens a suggestion.

formation_reference_en: Noun + でも
meaning_reference_en: or something (softening a suggestion)
notes_reference_en: Offers one example while leaving other options open, which makes invitations and advice sound less pushy.

formation_reference_en: i-Adj stem + さ / na-Adj + さ
meaning_reference_en: -ness (turns an adjective into a noun of degree)
notes_reference_en: いい becomes よさ. Common for measurements (高さ, 重さ, 大きさ, 長さ).

formation_reference_en: Noun (number + counter) + 目
meaning_reference_en: -th (ordinal: first, second, third ...)

formation_reference_en: Noun (number + counter) + おきに
meaning_reference_en: every other; at intervals of
notes_reference_en: With days (一日おき) it skips one unit, meaning 'every other day'. With minutes or distances it usually just means 'every X'.

formation_reference_en: i-Adj-ku + する / na-Adj + に + する / Noun + に + する
meaning_reference_en: make (something) ...; change something to a state
notes_reference_en: Someone deliberately changes something. Compare 〜くなる / 〜になる, where the change happens by itself.

formation_reference_en: Noun + がする
meaning_reference_en: (a smell, sound, taste or feeling) is perceived
notes_reference_en: Used with におい, 音, 声, 味 and 気 (〜気がする: 'have a feeling that').

formation_reference_en: Verb-plain / i-Adj / na-Adj / Noun + かな / かしら
meaning_reference_en: I wonder
notes_reference_en: A soft question, often said to oneself. かしら sounds feminine and a little old-fashioned. 〜ないかな can express a wish (早く来ないかな).

pattern: 〜てくれませんか / 〜ていただけませんか
romaji: te kuremasen ka / te itadakemasen ka
formation_reference_en: Verb-te + くれませんか / Verb-te + いただけませんか
meaning_reference_en: could you please ...? (polite request)
notes_reference_en: Softer than 〜てください. Politeness rises from 〜てくれませんか to 〜てもらえませんか to 〜ていただけませんか.

formation_reference_en: Verb-nai + で
meaning_reference_en: without doing; instead of doing
notes_reference_en: 〜ずに (N3) means the same but is more formal. Differs from 〜なくて, which gives a reason.
